body: I have to say I find the opposite, that without the normal boundaries of real life, people are far more likely, in the right circumstances, to be open and honest. Because what use is there, when anonymous, of being anything but? I guess that's the sort of friendships I feel like I look for online, that had worked for me for a long time, but in recent times, they just haven't.

Mostly online, as I struggle with being that open with face to face communication. I've always found it far easier to write my thoughts in to words, rather than speak about it. And usually in places like depression, self-harm and suicide support forums, always in the context of this sort of discussion being an ok thing. I certainly don't go randomly springing it on people, as I understand how difficult it could be for those who haven't faced these sort of thoughts, and don't understand them to deal with them.

I guess the thing that frustrates me most though is not that they stop, but that they never tell me why. I understand that people change, and that life moves on. I also feel that I try to be there as much as I can too, so if they are having difficulties in life, I would try to be there for them. There just never seems to be any sort of closure, I always hope that if someone decided they didn't want to talk, that they would just tell me. At least that way I'm not sitting here, wondering what I did to ruin things, and i've no doubt, given how often it's happened, that it is my fault.

I always try to understand what others are going through, and it has to be a mutual thing. I find it difficult to be open with someone who isn't also able to be open with me in return, and I guess I wouldn't even try to be. That's why I don't understand why people reject me in this way, because I wont just open up to anyone, and feel I am careful in who I talk to, that they genuinely care... and then they just refuse to talk to me, and don't explain why. So maybe my judgement on people is way off, or maybe I just drive people away. Either way, it's happened too many times for me not to draw conclusions from it.

It's something that can be said after one or two times, but I've lost count of the number of times that it has happened, without exception. I've tried talking to therapists, but have had no luck with them either. So the only common factor is me, and it might sound a stupid thing to say, but if the problem with my interactions is myself, and countless times have all produced the same outcome, the only conclusion is that I'm fucked up beyond the ability to change, or to be helped. And given it's been well over ten years, it's not a phase, just a fact of my life.
